SoK: Decentralized Finance (DeFi) - Fundamentals, Taxonomy and Risks (June 2023 draft)
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: June 2023 ACM-submitted draft; received 1 June 2023; placeholder DOI. Selected December 2022 categories cover claimed 89.09% TVL. Distinct version from later 2024 arXiv source.

nodes.label: DeFi value proposition taxonomy
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Trading: DEX and DEX aggregators. Lending: interest-rate pools and crypto-backed stablecoin CDPs. Asset management: yield farming and liquid staking. Interoperability: bridges.

nodes.label: Token taxonomy
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Technology facet separates native from smart-contract-enabled tokens; underlying-value facet distinguishes network, asset-backed and share-like categories.

nodes.label: Native blockchain tokens
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Native Layer 1 tokens; figure examples Bitcoin and Ether.

nodes.label: Smart-contract-enabled tokens
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Contract-issued tokens classified by underlying value.

nodes.label: Network-value tokens
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Governance and utility demand; figure example MakerDAO.

nodes.label: Asset-backed tokens
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Contains on-chain participation/LP tokens, synthetic assets, and real-world assets.

nodes.label: On-chain participation and LP receipt tokens
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Text uses on-chain asset and AMM participation; figure labels LP Tokens and gives aDAI/cDAI lending receipt examples. Preserve this granularity difference.

nodes.label: Synthetic tokens and synthetic-issuance protocols
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Derivative-like claims referencing another value: stablecoins, wrapped tokens, liquid staking; summary adds index tokens. Token entity and issuance mechanism must remain distinguishable in a language model.

nodes.label: Real-world-asset-backed tokens
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Off-chain backing, figure USDT example; crypto-backed protocols may indirectly depend on such assets through reserves.

nodes.label: Share-like tokens
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Source says value generated by holder/issuer work, illustrated with NFT art/CryptoPunks. Not a general legal equity classification.

nodes.label: DeFi algorithm taxonomy
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Three organizing mechanism families: liquidity pools, aggregators, synthetic issuance. Fig. 5 separately places CeFi under on-chain/off-chain settlement; order-book placement conflicts with some prose.

nodes.label: Liquidity-pool protocols
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Peer-to-pool supply/demand for token exchange or loanable funds. CLOB inclusion in prose is ambiguous relative to §3.1 and Fig. 5.

nodes.label: AMM decentralized exchanges
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Constant sum, constant product, weighted constant mean, StableSwap amplification; concentrated-liquidity intervals and translated virtual reserves. AMM versus CLOB must not be collapsed.

nodes.label: Interest-rate and loanable-funds protocols
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Linear, nonlinear and kinked utilization-dependent rates; supplied/borrowed liquidity, collateral, liquidation threshold, reserve factor. Flash loans use transaction atomicity. Zero-liquidation loans add tenor and optional redemption.

nodes.label: Aggregator protocols
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: DEX execution routing or yield allocation; accumulate risks of protocols and tokens they utilize.

nodes.label: DEX aggregators
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Optimize trade routing across fragmented pools. Source gives 21.5% routed volume here but 25% at p. 3 without aligned snapshot.

nodes.label: Yield farming and yield aggregators
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Simple lending; recursively leveraged borrowing; AMM liquidity provisioning. Fees/reward tokens and management/performance fees. Fig. 5 strategy boxes lack visible connectors; prose supplies parent relationship.

nodes.label: Stablecoin designs
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Fiat/off-chain collateral (CeFi); crypto-backed/on-chain overcollateralized CDP; algorithmic/noncollateralized supply adjustment via rebasing or seigniorage. Classification of rebasing as stablecoin acknowledged disputed.

nodes.label: Liquid-staking token designs
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Rebasing quantities (stETH), reward-bearing exchange value (wstETH/mSol/rETH), dual principal/reward tokens (sETH2/rETH2). Validator selection: whitelist, credentials, collateral. Depeg and slashing exposure.

nodes.label: Bridges and wrapped tokens
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Wrapped-token, liquidity-network, hybrid designs. Verification: external validators/federations versus light clients/relayers. Separate trusted, Binded [sic], insured, trustless labels remain underexplained. Not all bridges necessarily mint claims.

nodes.label: DeFi network-architecture taxonomy
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Single-chain, independent multichain deployments, cross-chain transfer, protocol-specific app-chain. These are source categories, not proven disjoint types.

nodes.label: Single-chain deployment
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Operates on one chain; figure example PancakeSwap.

nodes.label: Independent multichain deployment
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Multiple independent deployments without cross-chain value use; figure Uniswap/Lido and prose Aave/Uniswap.

nodes.label: Cross-chain value transfer
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Value crosses chains through interoperability; WBTC/Multichain examples.

nodes.label: Application-specific chain
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Protocol-specific sovereign chain; source distinguishes L1/L2/L3 security models. ThorChain/dYdX examples. Independent of whether transfers cross other chains.

nodes.label: DeFi stakeholder roles
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Customers: profit/credit/rewards. LPs: provide capital for fee/reward participation. Arbitrageurs: price-efficiency profit. Governance users: design/maintain and governance appreciation. Same actor may have multiple roles (inference).

nodes.label: DeFi risk and attack classification
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Risk depends on agent, protocol, and token; economic, infrastructure, smart-contract and application layers. Matrix is qualitative, not safety proof.

nodes.label: Economic DeFi risks
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Rug pull, slippage, impermanent loss, liquidation, depeg. Table/text differ on some exposures; source claims of immunity require assumptions. Depeg affects holders of synthetics and LP positions involving them.

nodes.label: Infrastructure attacks and MEV
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Blockchain consensus/timestamp attacks and transaction ordering: front-running, back-running, sandwich. Congestion affects execution; source broad claims about losses and prevention are not universal guarantees.

nodes.label: Smart-contract layer attacks
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Coding faults, untrusted external calls and access control. Audit/bounty defenses are cited, not independently reproduced.

nodes.label: Oracle price manipulation
nodes.author: Krzysztof Gogol; Christian Killer; Malte Schlosser; Thomas Bocek; Burkhard Stiller
nodes.rationale: Flash loan, AMM price distortion, collateral borrowing using manipulated AMM oracle, repayment/profit. Source cites broad role exposure; exact risks require price provenance.

nodes.rationale: Cited source of yield strategy algorithms and DeFi primitives. Citation only; not read separately.

nodes.label: SoK: DeFi Lending and Yield Aggregation Protocol Taxonomy, Empirical Measurements, and Security Challenges
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: Same bytes as prior SRC-0087; deeper source coverage is not independent corroboration.

nodes.label: Collateral-based loan family
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: Table II groups overcollateralized, undercollateralized and zero-liquidation designs; these facets need not be disjoint.

nodes.label: Overcollateralized lending
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: Collateral exceeds debt; price changes and interest growth can make positions eligible for liquidation.

nodes.label: Undercollateralized lending
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: Table II labels undercollateralized loans collateral-based; TrueFi prose includes loans without collateral. Historical Maple and TrueFi examples need contextual interpretation.

nodes.label: Zero-liquidation term loans
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: No early liquidation; at maturity repay with interest or forfeit collateral. High collateral/rates compensate risk without eliminating loss. MYSO is the example.

nodes.label: Flashloans
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: No collateral; available liquidity limits principal; fees are principal-based rather than time-based; atomicity qualifies the no-default claim.

nodes.label: Flashswaps
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: Repayment can use the other AMM pool asset; constant-product example x*y=k is stylized and needs fee-aware settlement rules.

nodes.label: Transaction-scoped repayment or revert
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: The introduction and repeated single-transaction wording support transaction atomicity. Section III-B also contains inconsistent same-block and transaction-sequence wording; shared timestamps do not establish joint rollback.

nodes.label: Pool utilization
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: Borrowed funds divided by available funds; U in [0,1]. Exact denominator and empty-pool behavior are not formalized.

nodes.label: Borrow and supply rate models
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: Borrower versus supplier rates, fixed versus dynamic updates, and rate-setting authority are separate choices.

nodes.label: Linear interest curve
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: Borrow rate alpha+beta*U.

nodes.label: Kinked interest curve
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: Continuous piecewise curve; gamma is upper-branch slope in formula although prose calls it slope increase. Steeper upper branch requires gamma>beta.

nodes.label: Nonlinear interest curve
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: alpha*U+beta*U^b+gamma*U^c; dYdX illustration uses powers 32 and 64.

nodes.label: Reserve factor and loss buffer
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: Supply rate example ib*U*(1-lambda); reserves can absorb losses, with tradeoffs for lender return and protocol finances.

nodes.label: Timestamp-based interest measurement
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: AAVE is described measuring elapsed time through block timestamps; source warns timestamps can be inaccurate under relevant blockchain assumptions.

nodes.label: Block-count interest measurement
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: Compound is described counting blocks under an assumed fixed inter-block interval; actual block-production timing can differ.

nodes.label: Lazy interest accrual
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: AAVE description materializes accrued interest when actions read or modify balances; not a complete version-specific implementation specification.

nodes.label: Liquidation eligibility and execution
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: Threshold breach permits liquidation but profit-seeking actors must execute it; partial liquidation and delays matter.

nodes.label: First-come-first-served liquidation
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: Speed and transaction ordering determine capture; liquidators may finance repayment with flashloans.

nodes.label: Auction liquidation
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: Auction delays execution but can improve protocol recovery by rewarding bids that take less collateral.

nodes.label: Type I bad debt
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: Collateral is worth less than debt, potentially after delayed liquidation.

nodes.label: Type II bad debt
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: Liquidation reward falls below transaction cost; changing fees can make execution profitable again.

nodes.label: Yield farming user strategy
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: Users deploy capital to earn interest, fees and rewards. Explicitly distinguished from protocol type.

nodes.label: Yield aggregator protocol
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: Automates strategies across underlying venues; dependency footprint includes lending markets, DEX pools, bridges and oracles.

nodes.label: Aggregator vault
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: Pooled funds use automated strategies and shared transaction costs; users can choose multiple vaults.

nodes.label: Receipt-token claims
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: AMM LP tokens or interest-bearing lending tokens represent claims redeemable for underlying assets/rewards; AAVE aTokens are an example.

nodes.label: Harvesting and reinvestment
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: Vault yields are reinvested through transactions; pooled investors share the gas cost.

nodes.label: Governance parameters and voting
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: Community token voting updates protocol policy; slower evaluation can conflict with urgent collateral-risk response.

nodes.label: Interest-rate manipulation
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: Mining-rate changes and liquidity-supply changes can distort accrual, rate comparisons and lending profits.

nodes.label: Governance issuance and recursive lending
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: Borrow/deposit rewards can offset borrowing cost and motivate repeated positions; borrowed voting tokens can sway governance.

nodes.label: Proof-of-stake timing research direction
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: Skipped production slots can separate consecutive block timestamps; combining timing manipulation with RANDAO manipulation is proposed future research, not reproduced evidence.

nodes.label: Revenue-based financing
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: Proposed repayment from an income fraction without collateral; income visibility and diversion are unresolved enforcement problems.

nodes.label: Compound V2 and AAVE V2 event measurements
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: Historical Ethereum windows end Jan2024; event/address entities are not individual loans/users. Collection and findings were read, not reproduced.

nodes.label: Aggregator TVL and APY snapshots
nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: August2022/January2025 market snapshots do not establish causality. Table VIII APY label % per 30D conflicts with annual-yield prose; heterogeneous sources are not normalized.

nodes.author: Arad Kotzer; Tom Azoulay; Yoad Abels; Aviv Yaish; Ori Rottenstreich
nodes.rationale: Contract exploits, volatile and illiquid collateral, slippage, oracle and bridge exposure constrain safe lending and aggregation.

nodes.label: Typed financial-obligation graph
nodes.rationale: Separate financial function, mechanism, claim, interface, deployment, dependencies and risk; brands may occupy several nodes.

nodes.label: Smallest economically meaningful classification object
nodes.rationale: Classify reserves, markets, pools, vaults, tokens, positions, strategies or deployments before brands.

nodes.label: FF.MNY: Money, payments, settlement
nodes.rationale: Issuance, redemption, transfer and settlement of money-like obligations.

nodes.label: FF.EXE: Exchange, price discovery, execution
nodes.rationale: Exchange existing claims or arrange trade execution.

nodes.label: FF.CRD: Credit, lending, collateral
nodes.rationale: Present liquidity against repayment, collateral or default obligations.

nodes.label: FF.CAP: Capital formation, treasury
nodes.rationale: Raise, issue or allocate new organizational/project capital.

nodes.label: FF.DER: Derivatives, contingent claims
nodes.rationale: Payoff depends on a price, rate, event, funding stream, maturity or future state.

nodes.label: FF.AMG: Asset management, vault systems
nodes.rationale: Continuing delegated portfolio allocation or strategy execution.

nodes.label: FF.SEC: Staking, security services
nodes.rationale: Capital compensated for consensus or security-service participation.

nodes.label: FF.RSK: Risk transfer, loss allocation
nodes.rationale: Explicit payment or capitalization to absorb specified losses of another.

nodes.label: Mechanism facet
nodes.rationale: AMM, order book, auction, solver, lending, rate, liquidation or tranche mechanisms describe how obligations work.

nodes.label: Asset and claim facet
nodes.rationale: Direct assets, reserves, shares, debt, staking receipts, derivatives, wrapped assets and legal claims are independent descriptions.

nodes.label: Funding and return source facet
nodes.rationale: Record borrower interest, trading fees, security rewards, derivative funding, external income, premiums and subsidy.

nodes.label: Lifecycle and liquidity facet
nodes.rationale: Represent atomic, synchronous, queued, epoch, request/claim, maturity and conditional redemption states.

nodes.label: Interface and standards facet
nodes.rationale: Distinguish implements, accepts, adapts, wraps and common co-use.

nodes.label: Execution and deployment facet
nodes.rationale: Single-chain, rollup, app-chain, multichain, off-chain matching and cross-chain execution differ.

nodes.label: Authority and trust facet
nodes.rationale: Admission, curator, oracle, admin, upgrade, pause, freeze, forced transfer and legal/custodial powers.

nodes.label: Dependencies and risk facet
nodes.rationale: Trace tokens, protocols, vaults, oracles, bridges, solvers, custodians, issuers, legal vehicles, sequencers and governance.

nodes.label: Stablecoin claim property
nodes.rationale: Stable value target alone does not identify backing or issuer function.

nodes.label: Vault container and accounting pattern
nodes.rationale: Vault terminology or ERC-4626 support alone does not establish delegated asset management.

nodes.label: RWA provenance and legal-trust facet
nodes.rationale: External asset provenance and legal/trust structure do not identify a financial function.

nodes.label: Aggregator routing and composition role
nodes.rationale: Routing/composition differs from continuing delegated capital management.

nodes.label: Function-specific metrics and recursive TVL
nodes.rationale: Use function-specific metrics; recursive receipts can count the same economic capital repeatedly.

nodes.label: Economic return attribution
nodes.rationale: Attribute cash flows, transfer payments, subsidies, fees and losses to their sources; wrappers do not manufacture underlying yield.

nodes.label: Typed standards and dependency relationships
nodes.rationale: Distinguish IMPLEMENTS, EXTENDS, REQUIRES, ACCEPTS_ASSET, ADAPTS_TO, WRAPS, ISSUES, BACKED_BY, REDEEMS_FOR, YIELD_FROM, DEPENDS_ON, GOVERNED_BY, AUTHORIZED_BY, PRICED_BY, SETTLES_ON and MESSAGES_VIA.

nodes.label: Interface compatibility
nodes.rationale: Syntactic callable interface does not establish behavioral or economic suitability.

nodes.label: Behavioral compatibility
nodes.rationale: Callbacks, rebasing, transfer fees and malicious ABI look-alikes can violate caller assumptions.

nodes.label: Economic compatibility
nodes.rationale: Claim, liquidity and risk semantics must suit the consuming protocol.

nodes.label: Orthogonal risk overlay
nodes.rationale: Separate implementation, interface, oracle, credit, lifecycle, authority, dependency, execution, legal and atomicity axes.

nodes.label: Atomicity of exploitation and settlement
nodes.rationale: Distinguish transaction/bundle boundaries from eventual cross-chain settlement; flash capital does not identify root vulnerability.

nodes.label: Independent standards evidence dimensions
nodes.rationale: Separate formal status, implementation maturity, deployment evidence, adoption and security evidence; Final does not prove safety or usage.

nodes.label: Revision-sensitive standards semantics
nodes.rationale: A standard number does not identify historical semantics; report uses ERC-7683 revisions as motivating case.

nodes.label: EIP-1 standards process
nodes.rationale: Distinguishes ERC from Core/Networking/Interface; requires is a normative dependency relation.

nodes.label: ERC-20 fungible interface
nodes.rationale: Balances/transfers/allowances do not establish backing, solvency, redemption or stable value.

nodes.label: ERC-4626 vault accounting
nodes.rationale: Distinguishes ideal conversions, previews, maxima and state transitions; accounting value is not exit liquidity.

nodes.label: ERC-7540 asynchronous requests
nodes.rationale: Extends ERC-4626 with pending, claimable and claimed lifecycle; asynchronous paths modify synchronous preview assumptions.

nodes.label: ERC-7575 multi-asset topology
nodes.rationale: Multiple asset-specific entry points may share an external share token; vault and share contract need not coincide.

nodes.label: ERC-7535 native-asset vault
nodes.rationale: Native-asset adaptation is separate from asynchronous lifecycle and multi-asset topology.

nodes.label: ERC-3156 flash liquidity
nodes.rationale: Callback and same-transaction repayment standardizes atomic liquidity capability, not a financial sector.

nodes.label: ERC-7683 solver-facing resolution
nodes.rationale: Report claims current Draft solver-facing eth_call resolution supersedes earlier escrow/fill lifecycle design; not independently verified here.

nodes.label: ERC-7786 generic cross-chain messaging
nodes.rationale: Gateway messaging does not establish common trust/finality guarantees.

nodes.label: ERC-7802 cross-chain mint/burn
nodes.rationale: Authorized mint/burn interface does not establish safe bridge authorization or counterpart deployment.

nodes.label: ERC-3668 off-chain retrieval
nodes.rationale: Retrieval and verification callbacks do not establish financial data truth.

nodes.label: ERC-3643 identity and compliance architecture
nodes.rationale: Identity/compliance-registry architecture does not itself establish legal compliance.

nodes.label: ERC-7943 RWA transfer controls
nodes.rationale: Eligibility, freezing and forced transfer do not encode the underlying legal/custodial claim.

nodes.label: Uniswap v4 pool and hooks
nodes.rationale: Report classifies pool as EXE and hooks as configurable supporting mechanisms.

nodes.label: CoW Protocol batch
nodes.rationale: Solver/combinatorial batch auction is exchange beyond pool-centric taxonomy.

nodes.label: Aave V3 reserve
nodes.rationale: Pooled collateralized variable-rate credit depends on oracle, liquidation and available withdrawal liquidity.

nodes.label: Morpho Blue market
nodes.rationale: Isolated credit parameters include loan asset, collateral, oracle, LLTV and interest-rate model.

nodes.label: Morpho Vault V2
nodes.rationale: Curated allocation uses adapters over markets; ERC-4626 share accounting differs from borrower interest and exit liquidity.

nodes.label: Liquity V2 Trove and BOLD issuance
nodes.rationale: Separate borrower collateralized debt, issuance through borrowing and circulating BOLD claim.

nodes.label: Ethena USDe
nodes.rationale: Money-like token uses crypto backing and derivatives hedges, with counterparty/custodial and access dependencies.

nodes.label: Pendle SY wrapper
nodes.rationale: Normalizes an underlying yield-bearing asset; does not create underlying yield.

nodes.label: Pendle PT principal claim
nodes.rationale: Principal right depends on maturity and underlying claim.

nodes.label: Pendle YT yield claim
nodes.rationale: Pre-maturity yield rights arise from underlying economic activity.

nodes.label: Lido stETH
nodes.rationale: Rebasing staking receipt depends on validators, oracle, withdrawals and slashing.

nodes.label: Lido wstETH
nodes.rationale: Non-rebasing share wrapper preserves dependence on underlying stETH staking system.

nodes.label: Ondo OUSG
nodes.rationale: External fund/security claim depends on eligibility, custody, legal rights and redemption conditions.

nodes.label: Centrifuge async and multi-asset vaults
nodes.rationale: Report describes ERC-7540 lifecycle and ERC-7575 topology as separate properties.

nodes.label: Nexus Mutual cover
nodes.rationale: Risk transfer with human/expert adjudication and membership dependencies.

nodes.label: GMX perpetual market
nodes.rationale: DER and EXE combine oracle pricing, leverage, pooled liquidity and execution dependencies.

nodes.label: Across cross-chain intent
nodes.rationale: Origin escrow, destination relayer capital and later settlement remain non-atomic across chains.
